column3: Directly confirms that the Hour is coming without doubt and joins it to resurrection.
Its stabilization against yielding is not an interpretive extension of the concealed Hour or reckoned striving.
Sets hidden and disclosed inner content under divine knowledge, clarifying the disclosure horizon.
States that every soul is repaid for what it earned, with no injustice.
The immediate continuation warns against being turned from the Hour by one who disbelieves in it.
Shows a soul satisfied with its striving, supplying a positive outcome for reckoned effort.
Links the true creation of heaven and earth to each soul's just recompense for what it earned.
The request for ease in Moses's affair does not develop the focus's Hour, concealment, or recompense.
Nearly restates the individual measure: a person has only what he strove for.
Reiterates that the Hour is certainly coming, while foregrounding widespread disbelief in it.
The polemical claim about Moses's low status and unclear speech is outside the focus's concern.
Affirms that nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from God, a broad basis for concealed timing and disclosure.
Concentrates knowledge of the Hour with God and pairs it with each soul's unknowing of its own future earning and death.
Its quiet discussion of duration belongs to the later Hour scene but adds little to the focus's stated relation.
Explicitly levels concealed and public speech and action before divine awareness.
Pairs a hidden reserve of recompense with deeds, closely extending concealedness and return for action.
Makes every soul receive in full what it earned on the Day of Resurrection.
Names the return as recompense and says the recipients' striving is acknowledged.
The staff's literal movement offers only a secondary contrast with purposeful human striving.
Moses's request for a helper does not illuminate the focus.
Extends concealment to what is within selves and makes it subject to divine accounting.
Places every being as individually arriving on the Day of Resurrection.
The statement of the Book's descent has no specific relation to the concealed Hour or recompense.
Its striving for corruption supplies only a contrary moral direction for the focus's striving.
The illusory movement attributed to magic is a distant contrast to the focus's purposeful striving.
The magicians' accusation and political fear do not add to the focus.
Contrasts displayed and concealed charity while retaining divine awareness of action.
Describes the Hour as near as a glance or nearer, sharpening its impending arrival.
The designation of a clear Book does not develop the focus's themes.
Its concealed call offers another mode of hidden address, though not the hidden timing of the Hour.
Directly joins what is exposed or concealed to God's comprehensive knowledge.
The throne declaration is adjacent-surah context without a specific relation to the focus.
Depicts striving toward corruption and its consequence, a contrary use of the action register.
The measure of financial obligation does not clarify the individual recompense for striving.
The nearly disclosed secret and its restraint provide a limited concealment parallel.
Its arriving in haste concerns summoned birds rather than the focus's human striving or the Hour.
The coming of death and ensuing punishment gives only a broad impending-end parallel.
Aaron's explanation of preserving communal unity is unrelated to the focus.
Describes a messenger disclosing much that had been concealed from the Book.
The warning scene implies an arriving messenger but does not specifically extend the focus.
The divine record that neither errs nor forgets is a limited backdrop for the focus's reckoning.
Its destructive striving supplies a contrary orientation, without the focus's reckoning formulation.
The Day of presentation leaves no hidden thing concealed.
Names God knower of the unseen and witnessed, broadly grounding the focus's concealment.
Connects hostile striving against the signs with a defined final consequence.
Contrasts doubt about the Hour with disclosure of deeds and severe recompense.
Names enduring gardens as the recompense of one who purifies himself.
The call made in concealment supplies a distinct but meaningful hiddenness parallel.
States that a person's striving will later be seen.
Moses's prayer for provision does not add to the focus.
The man's hurried arrival is a narrative use of striving, not the focus's reckoned human effort.
The argument about divine power over life and the sun has no focused connection here.
The command to worship and establish prayer is nearby context but does not explain the focus's concealed Hour.
The person's coming in haste is only a generic movement parallel.
The expression for a time of hardship is not the eschatological Hour of the focus.
The challenge for evidence about associates does not develop the focus.
Pairs God's bringing out what is hidden with knowledge of what people conceal and disclose.
The speaker's near ruin is not a useful extension of the focus.
The humbled faces and failed bearer of wrongdoing give a nearby final-account scene.
Specifies divine knowledge of furtive eyes and what breasts conceal.
Sets corrupt striving against a specified recompense in this world and the next.
The light parable does not specifically explain the focus's hiddenness or reckoning.
Joins intending the Hereafter and striving for it to acknowledged striving.
Directly states that God repays every soul for what it earned.
The source of the revelation is surrounding context rather than an extension of the focus.
Declares that human striving is diverse, adding a differentiation of the effort to be reckoned.
Presents each soul pleading for itself and receiving in full what it did.
The promised rewards to believers are a general recompense parallel without the focus's individual formulation.
Supplication in concealment offers a distinct hiddenness parallel.
Assigns every soul a guardian, supporting individual accountability.
The command to await an arriving day gives only a broad future-event parallel.
Commands purposeful movement toward remembrance, a concrete directed form of striving.
States that knowledge of the Hour belongs to God and stresses its possible nearness.
The domestic choice set before the wives does not illuminate the focus.
The man's hurried arrival and call to follow messengers is only a narrative movement parallel.
The demand for unrolled sheets does not develop the focus.
The sign of suspended speech is a different form of concealment without a focused link.
Its furtive looking in a Day-of-Resurrection scene gives a secondary concealment and final-account parallel.
Makes every soul pledged for what it earned.
The private complaint of bodily frailty does not extend the focus.
Portrays the day when all are exposed and nothing about them is hidden from God.
Shows each community called to its record and repaid for what it did.
The legal ordering of kinship does not clarify the focus.
Moves from something concealed within the self to what God brings forth, in a distinct context.
States that every soul is paid in full for what it did, under complete divine knowledge.
Places remembrance of what one strove for on the decisive Day.
Its collective abiding in the fire provides only a broad final-outcome parallel.
Describes previously concealed matter becoming manifest, though in a contrary response to disclosure.
Directly treats the Hour's concealed knowledge, its heaviness, and its sudden arrival.
Shows striving as deliberate movement in turning away, a contrary direction for the focus's effort.
The repeated recompense of those who do good is a concise general counterpart.
Names a garden and silk as recompense for patience, a specific but secondary return for conduct.
The giving of the clear Book does not develop the focus.
The recollection of Jesus's signs and their dismissal as magic is outside the focus's relation.
The command to give relatives their due does not clarify the focus.
Abraham's withdrawal after a promise is shown false does not develop the focus.
The divine address to Moses is not an interpretive extension of the focus.
The challenge to produce associates does not add to the concealed Hour or reckoning.
The statement of divine dominion and power is too general to extend the focus.
The statement of human weakness does not develop the focus.
Directly joins the unquestionable gathering Day to every soul receiving in full what it earned.
States that every soul will taste death and receive its wages in full on the Day of Resurrection.
Establishes that God does not wrong even the weight of an atom and multiplies good, sharpening just recompense.
Affirms the gathering on the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.
Depicts the meeting with God arriving suddenly after its denial.
Assigns degrees according to deeds and confirms that God is not heedless of what people do.
Specifies multiplied return for good and proportionate return for evil without injustice.
Places the weighing of deeds on the Day as the criterion of success.
Makes light scales the criterion of loss through wrongdoing.
Declares that deeds will be seen by God, the messenger, and believers before return to the Knower of unseen and witnessed.
Reserves the unseen to God and directs waiting for what its disclosure will bring.
Frames the demanded promise as an appointed time that cannot be advanced or delayed.
Sets the reality of the coming punishment against doubts and says it cannot be escaped.
Describes people concealing their breasts while God knows what they hide and what they reveal.
Names the Hour as something that may come suddenly while people are unaware.
Directly announces that the Hour is coming and calls for gracious forbearance until it does.
Announces the coming divine command and forbids treating it as something to hasten.
Binds each person's work to that person and promises an opened record on the Day of Resurrection.
Makes the individual self sufficient as the reckoner of its own account on that Day.
States that God knows best what is within selves, extending hidden interior content to judgment.
Uses the sleepers' case to affirm that the promise of God is true and the Hour has no doubt.
Shows the record leaving nothing small or great uncounted and finding deeds present.
Warns of the Day of Regret, when the matter is decided while people remain heedless.
Names God's knowledge of the secret and what is still more hidden.
Introduces the Day the Trumpet is blown and the guilty are gathered.
Declares that humanity's account has drawn near while people turn away in heedlessness.
Sets just scales for the Day of Resurrection so no soul is wronged, even by the weight of a seed.
Identifies the convulsion of the Hour as an immense event.
Warns that the Hour may come suddenly or that the barren Day may arrive.
Makes heavy scales the mark of successful souls.
Makes light scales the mark of souls who have lost themselves.
Connects the best recompense and increase to what people do.
Warns that the Hour may come suddenly upon those who oppose the command.
Sets the meeting with God at an appointed coming term.
Promises that those who believe and do good will have their evil deeds covered and receive the best return for what they did.
Places the guilty in despair on the Day the Hour is established.
Records doubt about a new creation after becoming lost in the earth, a direct resurrection horizon.
Explicitly says that the Hour will come and pairs it with the Knower of the unseen.
Defines an appointed Day that cannot be delayed or advanced.
Warns against being deceived about God's true promise.
Names God as Knower of the unseen of the heavens and earth and of what is within breasts.
Depicts the Trumpet blast and people emerging from graves toward their Lord.
Directly states that no soul is wronged and people are repaid only for what they did.
Shows that even all earthly possession could not ransom people from the evil that will appear to them on the Day.
Depicts the Trumpet blast, resurrection, and standing in expectation.
Reserves knowledge of the Hour to God and joins it to what emerges or is concealed in creation.
States that the Hour may be near.
Makes the sign a source of knowledge of the Hour and forbids doubt concerning it.
States that God gathers all at the Day of Resurrection, about which there is no doubt.
Contrasts treating the Hour as doubt with God's promise that it is true.
Describes the evil of deeds becoming apparent and punishment enclosing those who mocked it.
Assigns degrees according to deeds so that each may be paid in full without wrong.
Warns that people await only the Hour coming upon them suddenly.
Marks the blast as the arrival of the promised Day.
Makes God recompense those who do evil for what they did and reward those who do good with the best.
Declares that the Hour has drawn near.
Introduces the occurring Event whose occurrence cannot be denied.
Contrasts false hope and deception with the final separation on the Day of judgment.
Describes God raising all and informing them of what they did after deeds were counted though forgotten.
Joins God's knowledge of what is in heaven and earth to what people conceal and reveal and to what breasts contain.
Equates concealed and open speech before the Knower of what breasts hold.
Reports that people see the promised Day as distant.
Counters that divine sight sees the promised Day as near.
Places the human question about where to flee on that Day.
Says a person will be informed that Day of what was sent ahead and left behind.
Names the Day of Decision as an appointed time.
Begins the cosmic disclosure sequence when the sun is wrapped up.
Makes every soul know what it sent ahead and left behind.
Defines the Day when no soul can avail another and all command belongs to God.
Sets an unfailing reward for believers who do good.
Names the Day when secrets are tested.
Affirms divine knowledge of what is open and what is hidden.
Describes people issuing forth separately to be shown their deeds.
Makes even an atom's weight of good visible.
Makes even an atom's weight of evil visible.
Makes heavy scales the condition of a pleasant life.
Makes light scales the condition of a plunging abyss.
